Written answers (Short Answer and Long Answer) go through a layered grading pipeline. 
Step 1 is exact match after normalization, awarding full marks immediately if correct. 
Step 2 uses fuzzy match for short strings to catch minor typos.

p05.answer: Written answers are scored using a layered grading pipeline. First, the system checks for an exact match after normalizing the answer (lowercasing, trimming, removing punctuation). Full marks are awarded only if the answer matches at any stage of this pipeline.

c03.query: What is the difference between an Exam and an Arena game?
c03.expected: An Exam is asynchronous, individually timed, and includes detailed proctoring, with results sent to the Results tab and regular exam Monitoring tabs. In contrast, an Arena game is synchronous where everyone plays at the same time, uses speed-based scoring with streaks, is controlled by the host, and has its results saved to game history and a separate section in Analytics.
c03.answer:
**Exam**
- Asynchronous: students take it on their own schedule
- Individually timed per student
- Detailed proctoring and grading
- Results appear in the **Results** tab

**Arena game**
- Synchronous: everyone plays at the same time
- Host controls the pace
- Speed-based scoring with streaks
- No detailed proctoring
- Results go to **game history**, not the Exam Results tab
- Analytics appear in a separate **Analytics** workspace section
chunks:
[terminology] Common Confusions
Arena vs Exams: Arena is a live, synchronous game with speed scoring.
Exams are asynchronous, individually timed assessments with detailed
grading.

Notifications vs Email: Most notifications are in-app only. Quizzer
does not email about generation, attempts, integrity, or exports.
Email is only for signup verification, password reset, and exam share
invitations.

Draft (exam) vs Draft (question): An exam in Draft state means it is
unpublished. A question in Draft status means it has not been reviewed
yet. Different concepts sharing the same word.

## How Arena Differs from Graded Exams
Graded exams: asynchronous. Publish a link, students take it on their
own time, individually timed, detailed proctoring, graded results in
the Results tab.

Arena: synchronous. Everyone plays at the same time. Host controls the
pace. Speed-based scoring with streaks. No detailed proctoring.
Results go to game history, not the exam Results tab.

Arena packs do not appear in the regular exam Results or Monitoring
tabs. Arena analytics appear in a separate section of the Analytics
workspace.

t04.query: exam link not working for student
t04.expected: To troubleshoot a non-working exam link for a student, perform the following checks: first, verify that the exam is published and not unpublished or archived. Second, check if the link window (`available_until` time) has expired, and if so, extend or renew it from the Links tab. Third, confirm that the students are using the correct link provided from the Links tab.
t04.answer:
**Likely causes first, then UI checks:**

1. **Exam not published** — Unpublished or archived exams cannot be accessed. Confirm the exam status is **Published** in the Exams workspace.

2. **Link window expired** — Check the **available_until** date on the **Links** tab. If the window has passed, students will be blocked.

3. **Verification form required** — If the exam has a verification schema, students must complete all required fields before starting. Review **Verification schema** settings.

4. **Max attempts exhausted** — If **max attempts** is set and the student has used all allowed attempts, they cannot start again.

**UI checks (in order):**

- Open the **Exams** workspace → select the exam → verify the **Publish** action is active and all questions are approved on the **Questions** tab.
- Go to the **Links** tab and confirm the link is active and the **available_until** date has not passed.
- If verification is enabled, open the **Verification** tab and ensure the schema does not block entry.
- Check **Attempts** settings under the exam configuration to see if the student has reached the limit.

If none of these resolve the issue, contact support with the exam ID and student details.

Students say the link does not work:
First check: is the exam published? Unpublished or archived exams

[taking-exams] How Students Access an Exam
## How Students Access an Exam
The teacher publishes the exam and shares the link (via copy/paste,
email, Google Classroom, or QR code). Students open the link in a web
browser.

Requirements for the link to work:
- The exam must be published (not unpublished or archived)
- The link window must still be open (available_until not expired)
- If access codes are required, the student needs a valid unused code
- The student must not have exceeded the maximum attempts limit

Students do NOT find exams through the Quizzer website, a search, or
a dashboard listing. They ONLY access exams through links shared by
the teacher. Even students with Quizzer accounts cannot discover exams
on their own.

s06.query: How do I get better AI-generated questions in Quizzer?
s06.expected: Provide clear, well-structured source content with organized material, clear topics, and concepts.
s06.answer:
To improve AI-generated questions in Quizzer:

1. **Use Guided mode** — specify the exact number of questions, types (Multiple Choice, True/False, Short Answer, etc.), and structure you want.
2. **Provide high-quality source material** — paste text, upload a document (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, TXT), or share a YouTube/web page URL. The AI extracts questions from this content.
3. **Review and approve** — AI questions start as drafts. Use the **Review and approve** step to edit or discard any that don't meet your standards before publishing.

## Tips for Better AI Generation
Provide clear, well-structured source content. The AI generates better
questions from organized material with clear topics and concepts.

Use Guided mode when you need exact control. Source-first is convenient
but may not match your exact expectations for question count or type.

For best OCR results on scanned PDFs, ensure the scan is clean and
text is legible. Blurry or low-resolution scans produce poor text
extraction.

YouTube URLs work best when the video has good captions (manual or
auto-generated). Videos with poor audio or no captions may not produce
useful text.
